absent: Locking, concurrency and sleeping constraints for firmware node traversal, property reads and reference counting.
Error return codes and failure modes for property reads, counts and compatibility queries beyond delegation.
Memory ownership and lifetime rules for property external pointers, software nodes and connection match results.
PSCI transport, calling convention and state values beyond standby versus power down encodings.
SEV and SNP command sequences, firmware blob format and policy enforcement semantics.
Profiling data collection, buffering and tick handling beyond the no-operation stand ins.
Project identifier namespace mapping tables and permission checks beyond identity conversion.
Spin helper interaction with interrupts, preemption and architecture specific relaxation.

findings.text: Busy wait helper pauses the processor with relaxation hints while a caller supplied condition stays false, entering the relaxed loop only when the first check fails and leaving once the condition holds. No timeout or sleep occurs, so callers must guarantee eventual truth and that spinning is legal in the current context.
Profiling categories are distinct single bit values usable as a mask: processor sampling uses value one, scheduler sampling uses value two, virtualization sampling uses value four.

When profiling support is compiled out the header exposes neutral stand ins guarded by a single include marker. Creation and initialization report success, tick and multi hit recorders discard their arguments, and the single hit recorder also discards its arguments. The global enable indicator is a constant zero.

In the enabled configuration the single hit fast path compares the global enable indicator against the requested category and forwards to the multi hit recorder with a count of one only on equality, otherwise doing nothing. This keeps the common disabled case cheap.

Project identity has a raw thirty two bit numeric form and a kernel wrapper holding one value of that form. A small accessor reveals the wrapped number and a constructor builds a wrapper from a raw number. The header is protected by a single include marker.
Two reserved project identities are defined: an invalid marker built by wrapping all bits set, and an overflow fallback using decimal sixty five thousand five hundred thirty four.

Ordering and equality compare the unwrapped numbers, and validity means difference from the invalid marker. Conversion between raw and wrapped forms preserves the number while ignoring the namespace argument in these fragments. One mapping predicate treats all bits set as unmapped, another variant reports mapped unconditionally, and the munged conversion substitutes the overflow fallback when the raw result indicates unmapped.
Property value categories distinguish four unsigned integer widths from narrowest to widest together with a text category and a reference category for links to other nodes.

Firmware node endian detection reports big endian when an explicit marker property exists, or when the build targets big endian hardware and a native endian marker exists. Compatibility checks for presence of a supplied string inside the compatibility list. Device level wrappers obtain the firmware node of the device and delegate, as does the helper matching a property string against a table.

Parent and child traversal helpers repeatedly request the next related firmware handle starting from an initial lookup, yielding each handle in turn until none remains. Variants select only handles whose name matches, only handles marked available, device rooted traversals, and scoped forms that release each handle automatically after the iteration step.
Releasing a firmware handle dispatches its type specific put operation. Child population queries for a device delegate to the underlying firmware node, with a named variant filtering by name.

Single value numeric accessors for devices and firmware nodes request exactly one array element of the corresponding width, while population probes pass an empty buffer to learn length. String array population is probed the same way. Device forms forward to the device firmware node behavior.

A reference argument record pairs an optional static node pointer with an optional firmware handle, plus a count and a fixed capacity inline array of sixty four bit arguments for the link. A construction helper accepts either static node flavor or firmware handle flavor through type generic selection and tallies trailing variadic values into the inline array.

A software property record carries a name pointer, a byte length, an inline flag and a category tag. Storage is either an external pointer for larger data or an inline slot wide enough for a sixty four bit quantity, interpretable as narrow or wide integers or as text pointers depending on category.

Construction helpers build property records for integer widths, text and links. Array forms record length as element count times element width and keep an external pointer without setting the inline flag. Single value forms mark inline and store the value directly. Boolean form sets only name and inline flag. Reference forms accept either a prepared reference record or a node plus trailing arguments and store a pointer to the resulting reference record.
A static firmware node carries a name pointer, a link to its parent static node and a pointer to its property record list. A construction helper fills those three links from supplied arguments.
A firmware node counts as a graph endpoint when a remote endpoint marker property is present. Endpoint traversal repeatedly asks for the next endpoint starting from empty until none remains.
Graph traversal flags occupy the lowest two bits: the next endpoint request uses bit zero and the disabled device allowance uses bit one.

Device connection lookup forwards to firmware node matching using a caller supplied callback that receives a firmware handle and an identifier and returns an opaque pointer. The device wrapper resolves the firmware node and passes through connection id, caller data and callback.
Power state type encodings use zero for standby and one for power down.

A power controller operation table groups version query, suspend with state and entry address, power down, power up with identifier and entry address, relocation, affinity probe with two levels, and relocation type query. A separate legacy identifier record holds four thirty two bit function numbers for suspend, power up, power down and relocation.

Device tree and ACPI initialization helpers in this configuration report success without action, while presence and hypercall use indicators report false, signalling that no firmware interface is available.

A pseudofilesystem construction record aggregates pointers to filesystem operation tables for superblock, export, extended attributes and directory handling, together with a numeric magic value and directory entry flag bits.

Secure encrypted virtualization policy reserves single bit positions zero through five for debug denial, key sharing denial, encrypted state, send denial, domain and sev enablement, with major version occupying bits sixteen to twenty three and minor version occupying bits twenty four to thirty one.

Secure nested paging policy uses sixty four bit masks where minor version spans bits zero to seven and major spans eight to fifteen, singletons cover threading, must be one reserved, migration agent, debug, single socket, coherent link allowance, wide memory encryption, power reporting disable, DRAM ciphertext hiding and page swap disable, and a base aggregate combines the version fields with threading through single socket.
Firmware blob transfers are bounded to sixteen kibibytes, encoded as hexadecimal four thousand.
Firmware lifecycle advances from uninitialized through initialized to working, with numeric codes zero, one and two respectively and a terminal maximum marker delimiting the range.
